title: Fit an ISOFIX booster seat: click both connectors onto the car's anchors, then hold the adjust button and push it flat
instruction: Fit the booster seat to the car seat's ISOFIX anchors.
context: Parents and carers fit and refit ISOFIX child seats whenever a seat moves between cars or rows. An ISOFIX low anchorage is a 6 mm round steel bar in the gap between a car seat's cushion and backrest (UN Regulation No. 145); the two bars sit 280 mm apart. A high-back booster's manual (Britax Römer KIDFIX i-SIZE) has two steps: click both extended locking arms onto the bars, then use the ISOFIX adjustment button to slide the seat back until its backrest is flat against the car's; before each journey the green area must show on both arms. A seat latched on one side, or left standing off the backrest, looks fitted but is not.
setup: Positions in metres in the robot frame: x forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the robot's left of their midpoint. Table top 0.7475 m; the table spans x -0.19 to 0.91, y -0.65 to 0.65. (1) Car rear-seat stand-in, fixed (real build: plywood box with upholstery fabric): cushion 0.80 wide (y -0.40 to 0.40), x 0.15 to 0.79, top 40 mm above the table; backrest 0.10 thick and 0.515 tall, front face at x 0.79, starting 45 mm above the cushion so a 45 mm gap (the seat bight) is left under it, closed at the back (x 0.85 to 0.89). (2) Two ISOFIX anchorages in the bight: 6 mm round steel bars along y, centres at x 0.81, 20 mm above the cushion, y +-0.14, each inside a black plastic insertion guide (sleeve 36 mm wide, 34 mm tall inside, 3 mm walls, from the backrest face 30 mm in, mouth flared 6 mm per side over its first 10 mm). (3) High-back ISOFIX booster seat (KIDFIX i-SIZE type), plastic shell with fabric, dark grey, loose, 6.5 kg: seat cushion 0.44 wide, 0.36 deep, 0.10 tall; backrest 0.09 thick rising to 0.60 above its base, with a headrest; armrests 40 mm wide, 70 mm tall, from 60 to 340 mm in front of its back face. Locking-arm bracket: two 30 x 28 mm steel arms at y +-0.14 (booster frame) joined under the seat, pulled out 100 mm so each connector (8 mm slot, sprung catch plunger) reaches 145 mm behind the back face; locked where it is unless the ISOFIX adjustment button is held in (past 4 mm of its 8 mm stroke). Button: red, 60 x 25 mm, middle of the cushion's front face 20 mm below its top, 12 mm proud. A window on each armrest shows red until that side is latched, then green. Start: back edge centre at x 0.60, y 0 (190 mm from the backrest, 70 mm short of the connectors reaching the bars), turned 2 deg counterclockwise seen from above. Both arms at their ready pose, grippers open.
scoring: Latched, per side: the bar in its connector's throat (centre 17 to 25.5 mm behind the connector's reference; 20 mm when seated), within the 8 mm slot and 15 mm of the arm's line, with the catch down behind it (within 2 mm of its stop); the window shows green. Flush: the booster's back face within 5 mm of the backrest at both sides (20 mm in from its edges, 70 mm up). End state: 1.0 = both latched and flush, every finger pad at least 3 cm from the booster, booster at rest (under 5 mm/s and 0.05 rad/s); 0.75 = both latched and flush but held or moving; 0.5 = both latched, not pushed flat; 0.25 = one side only; 0 = neither. 0 for the rest of the trial if the booster tips over 30 deg or drops 20 mm off the cushion. Real trial: green on both arms, back gap by ruler, and a 50 N pull (luggage scale, 2 s) that moves it less than 5 mm.
run_limit: 1,600 steps (80 s at 20 Hz); the scripted demo is fitted by about step 600 and done by 810.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Press both connector release buttons and pull the booster off the bars, hold the adjustment button and pull the arms out 100 mm, and set the booster back at its start (the release buttons are not modelled in the simulation).
fidelity: Rigid bodies, PhysX 240 Hz. Rigid car seat, no foam; bars in an open bight. Both arms are one bracket; with the button out its slide is pinned where it is (the ratchet), held in it slides at 3 N. Each catch is a sprung plunger (40 N/m) the bar lifts on a ramp. The armrest window stands in for the arm's green area. Booster mass and sizes, connector, guide, button and friction 0.4 are estimates; 6 mm bars from UN R145, 280 mm the usual ISOFIX spacing.
